title: Still God, experiencing life within the rules
identity: Entering this game does not mean that we cease to be God. We are the same Creator who voluntarily entered different lives without unrestricted powers available to each individual role. The limitation belongs to the way the game is experienced; it does not remove our shared divine identity.
example: Why did we leave our powers behind? With unrestricted powers, there would be no experience to have: we would need no body, food, cars, houses, or anything else that gives everyday life its rich experiences. If everyone could create anything instantly, the game would collapse and nothing within it would have meaning. We voluntarily left those powers behind to live through the game’s needs, relationships, and limitations, while remaining the same Creator.
recognition: Remembering “I am the Creator” therefore means recognizing who is having the experience while continuing to live within the game’s rules. Recognizing this identity does not give the individual unrestricted powers or the ability to rewrite the design from inside. The same divine identity belongs to everyone, not only to the person who understands the teaching.
meditationTitle: Explore identity and the purpose of experience in meditation
meditation: Examine this truth through meditation and quiet reflection: if every power were available without limitation, what purpose would a body, a journey, or a relationship serve? What does it mean for the same Creator to experience life through a passing role? Meditation is a space for quiet self-enquiry, rather than an attempt to acquire supernatural powers.
question: Does entering the game mean that we are no longer God?
